 Order

The above writ petition is filed to declare the action of the respondents in taking possession of the land of the petitioners measuring 8 ft. abutting Araku-Visakhapatnam Road in Sy.No.23/1, NAD Kotha Road, Buchirajupalem, Visakhapatnam and in giving marks for taking possession of further extent land of the petitioners without any acquisition proceedings and without paying any compensation as illegal and arbitrary.
SRS, J 2. Heard Sri G.V. Shivaji, learned counsel for the petitioners and K. Madhava Reddy, learned standing counsel appearing for the 1st respondent.
3. Facts, in brief, are that the petitioners are the brothers.
Their houses are situated adjacent to each other in the land of an extent of Ac.0-32 cents in Sy.No.23/1, NAD Kotha Road, Visakhapatnam.
The land was originally purchased by the father of the petitioners through registered sale deed dated 29.04.1965.
The petitioners constructed houses and have been paying taxes regularly.
The 1st respondent Corporation took up road widening during the year 2006.
Nearly 8 ft. of the land belonged to the petitioners abutting the road was taken by the 1st respondent.

No compensation was paid to the petitioners.
Hence, the above writ petition is filed.
4. Counter affidavit was filed on behalf of the 1st respondent.
It was contended, inter-alia, that as per the remarks of Town Surveyor, about 6 to 10 feet of the land in Sy.No.23/1 of Butchirajupalem Village was involved in the BRTS road alignment.
In total, the property of the petitioners SRS, J was involved is an extent of 41 sq.mts in the proposed BRTS road alignment.
Except road widening portion, the 1st respondent Corporation did not give any marking to the petitioners' site for Bus bay as alleged.
The respondent Corporation would issue TDR certificates in lieu of the property affected in the proposed road widening.
5. As seen from the counter affidavit, there is no dispute that an extent of 41 sq.mts of the petitioners' property was involved in extension of BRTS road alignment.
However, compensation was not paid to the petitioners.
In the counter affidavit it was mentioned that, the respondent Corporation will issue TDR certificates in favour of the petitioners in lieu of the compensation.

6. Sri K. Madhava Reddy, learned standing counsel would submit that respondent Corporation will follow the procedure contemplated under Rules 167 and 168 of the Andhra Pradesh Building Rules,
2017.
It is submitted that notices will be issued calling upon the petitioners to execute gift deeds.
If the petitioners execute gift deeds, the Corporation will issue TDR certificates.
SRS, J 7.

Since the petitioners' land of an extent of 41 sq.mts is involved and the same is undisputed, as per the averments in the counter affidavit filed by the 1st respondent, the 1st respondent shall follow the procedure as per Rules 167 and 168 of the Andhra Pradesh Building Rules, 2017; the provisions of the Municipal Corporation Act 1955 and pass appropriate orders within a period of six (06) weeks.
8. With the above observation, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand dismissed.
__ JUSTICE SUBBA REDDY SATTI Date: 09.01.2024 KAS SRS, J THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE SUBBA REDDY SATTI Date: 09.01.2024 KAS P.Venkateswara Rao vs The Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal ...
